sb2038PrimarySourceCheck.claim: Dispatch card: SB 2038 (2023) created ETJ release by petition.
sb2038PrimarySourceCheck.finding: CONFIRMED via capitol.texas.gov/BillLookup/BillSummary.aspx?LegSess=88R&Bill=SB2038 and capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/88R/analysis/html/SB02038F.htm: SB 2038, 88th Legislature Regular Session (2023), added Subchapters D (direct petition) and E (petition by election) to Texas Local Government Code Chapter 42, effective 2023-09-01. A landowner-majority or resident petition can release land from a municipality's ETJ; failure to act within the statutory window releases the area by operation of law; a released area cannot re-enter ETJ or corporate limits without the owner's own later request. This is a real, citable statute -- the card's claim was not fabricated.
sb2038PrimarySourceCheck.secondaryFinding_SB1844: The 116 parcels in Austin's own GIS cite a DIFFERENT bill, SB 1844 -- verified this is 89th Legislature (2025), amending Local Government Code Sec. 43.141, effective 2025-09-01, expanding disannexation for property annexed but not receiving water/wastewater service near a navigable waterway. Per Austin's own council records (services.austintexas.gov/edims case documents) and reporting on the mechanism, land disannexed under SB 1844/Sec. 43.141 lands back IN the city's ETJ rather than being released from it -- consistent with those 116 rows carrying JURISDICTION_LABEL 'AUSTIN 2 MILE ETJ' rather than an 'outside all jurisdiction' code.
sb2038PrimarySourceCheck.mechanismConsidered: Two mechanisms could produce '116 rows cite SB 1844 inside the ETJ label': (a) Austin's attribute is a stale/incorrect citation and SB 2038 is what actually governs those rows -- REJECTED, because SB 2038 releases land FROM the ETJ entirely (an area released under it should not carry an ETJ jurisdiction label at all), while these 116 rows are still labeled ETJ, matching SB 1844/Sec 43.141's actual effect (full-purpose to ETJ, not ETJ to nothing). (b) SB 1844 and SB 2038 are two distinct, correctly-cited statutes governing two different transitions (full-purpose-to-ETJ vs ETJ-to-released) -- ACCEPTED, both bills independently verified live against capitol.texas.gov and Austin's own case records.
sb2038PrimarySourceCheck.relevanceToTheRulingNotBeingMade: A third real-world mechanism (Sec 43.141 water/wastewater disannexation) now joins the AG-development-agreement carve-outs already named in the dispatch as evidence that Austin's actual ETJ boundary is shaped by individual, one-off legal/administrative actions on named parcels, not a derivable §42.021 population-keyed formula. This strengthens, but does not decide, the case the dispatch already flagged as against a derived-ETJ approach. Not a ruling; carried forward as instructed.
